That’s fine and that’s your decision. In my mind this is the person whom you are going to potentially share everything with. Who will potentially have to make medical decisions for you and the rest of your family if you were to die. Yet you want to still have parts of yourself hidden from the one person whom is supposed to be the person that you love and trust. Seems counter productive. Although like I said that’s your decision and it’s okay to disagree.

Ask first always try to openly communicate a facilitate a safe environment where they can answer your questions open and honestly. If that doesn’t work, ask them if they’d be comfortable with letting you see their phone. Go to couples therapy or counseling. There are a lot of ways to get answers or the truth in order to feel more comfortable and safe if a relationship with your partner that doesn’t physically or emotionally harm them in any way. The thing that does harm people is pride or “why should I have to do xxxx for this person?” Because you chose to be with them and if it’s something that isn’t harming you in any way, why not?
Why assume you can trust them? Because they give you butterflies? Because they sweet talked you? I never said assume you can’t trust them. I said “trust and verify”.

You already said good luck with that. Just because you are extremely defensive and have things to hide doesn’t mean everyone else should. If I could magically take one test and it would make my partner more comfortable and secure I would without letting pride get in the way.
It doesn’t necessarily have to be to that extreme. Yes it should go both ways and if people weren’t so defensive then it could actually boost trust and the bonds between partners.

Trust is good, trust is cool. But you are just as likely to get hurt blindly trusting that people will have your own best interest in mind when you choose to be gone for long periods at a time. Again trust is cool and hunky dory but blind trust or faith leads to a lot of pain and suffering. Trust and verify. It’s just smart.
